claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified as launch-ready on aggregate operational evidence, so long as the current packet is framed as general readiness support and explicitly discloses that family placement prioritization for the named shelter-context deployment remains unevaluated.
decision_criteria: General readiness evidence can support launch-readiness claims only for the scope actually tested.
Named deployment-context evaluation gaps are material when the deployment plan specifically identifies that context.
Model-card certification must disclose material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
A verdict stronger than suspicious would require admissible evidence that the required disclosure or risk acceptance is already in place.
evidence_requests: Provide the final certification packet or model card showing explicit disclosure of the family-placement evaluation gap for the named deployment context.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance record authorizing launch before the missing family-placement evals are completed.
Provide the completed family placement prioritization evaluation results if they now exist.
Provide the final launch decision artifact showing how the named-context gap was handled under release policy.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports general launch readiness, but it also shows a named deployment-context evaluation gap for family placement prioritization.
The policy requires material limitations or evaluation gaps for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has actually been made in the certification materials.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering launch with the missing named-context evals.
The draft model card's statement that there are no known shelter-placement limitations is contradicted by QA's position that missing evals should be treated as unknown rather than passed.
unsupported_claims: Any clean certification claim that implies named shelter-context coverage is complete or passed.
Any representation that the absence of failed completed tests means there are no known limitations for emergency shelter placement.
Any claim that policy predicates for launch are fully satisfied without showing either explicit disclosure or approved risk acceptance for the named-context gap.
